desc:
Most security incidents come from known problems that nobody got round to fixing. Ecom Swift LLC provides SaaS security updates and access review: we patch known vulnerabilities in your app and check who can reach your code, servers and tools.

## What are SaaS security updates and an access review?

Security updates fix known weaknesses in the libraries and code your app relies on. An access review checks who and what can reach your systems: staff accounts, contractors, API keys, servers and third-party tools, and removes what is no longer needed.

Together they make up a focused security sprint. It is not a penetration test and not a formal audit. It is practical hardening of the basics that attackers most often use.

## Why basic security gaps matter

Attackers rarely begin with clever techniques. They scan for outdated packages with public fixes, keys committed to a repository, accounts of people who left long ago and admin pages with weak protection. These are cheap to find and cheap to use.

For a SaaS business the damage goes beyond the incident. Customers trust you with their data, and larger customers ask security questions before they sign. A single exposed key or unpatched library can cost a deal, a contract or a reputation that took a long time to build.

## How hardening reduces risk

Each fix closes a door. Patching a known vulnerability removes a method that automated tools already use. Removing an old account removes a login nobody is watching. Moving secrets out of the code into safe storage means a leaked repository no longer leaks your database. Tighter session and login settings make stolen credentials less useful.

The result is a smaller target and a clearer picture. Your team also learns what normal looks like, so unusual access becomes easier to spot. The outcome depends on your setup, and no sprint can make a system immune, but the common routes get blocked.

## What a focused security sprint includes

- A scan of your app and its libraries for known vulnerabilities.
- Patches for the issues that can be fixed safely, in priority order.
- A search for exposed keys, tokens and passwords in the code and its history.
- An access review for the repository, servers, hosting and admin tools.
- Removal of old accounts, unused keys and unneeded permissions.
- Tighter login, password and session settings.
- Security headers added to your web responses.
- A review of API and admin routes, in the larger package.
- Secrets moved to a proper storage place.
- A backup and restore check, and a one-page incident response plan.

## How we work

We start with a scan and a short interview about how your team works and who has access to what. We then patch what is safe to patch, one change at a time, with tests where they exist. For access, we produce a list of accounts and keys and agree with you which ones to remove.

The Basic package scans your app, patches the most serious issues, checks for exposed keys and gives you a short report. Standard adds the access review, removal of old accounts and keys, tighter login and session settings and security headers. Premium adds a wider set of fixes, a review of API and admin routes, safe secret storage, a backup check, an incident response plan and a team walkthrough.

If we find something serious, we tell you at once and do not wait for the final report.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Give us an honest list of everyone with access.
- Rotate any key we flag as exposed.
- Turn on two-factor sign-in for staff accounts.
- Keep a test copy for checking patches.
- Schedule regular updates after this sprint.

**Avoid:**
- Sending real customer data when test data will do.
- Sharing passwords in chat or email.
- Deleting history to hide an exposed key instead of rotating it.
- Assuming a small team is too small to be targeted.
- Treating this sprint as a compliance certificate.

## Who this is for

This suits a SaaS team that has never reviewed access since the first contractors left. It suits a founder facing a customer security questionnaire. It also suits a team that inherited a codebase and does not know what secrets it holds.

## What we need from you

Repository access as a collaborator or developer user, and read-only roles where we need to check hosting or tool settings. We do not need your passwords, and we do not need to see customer data to do this work. Anything sensitive we come across is reported to you privately.
